candidates.title: Off-chain send_cmio_response verifier accepts read accesses that carry written data and a written hash (inconsistent log data accepted)
candidates.component: Off-chain verifiers: replay_send_cmio_state_access::check_read (machine::verify_send_cmio_response, cm_verify_send_cmio_response, Lua machine:verify_send_cmio_response, JSON-RPC machine.verify_send_cmio_response); used by the referee model doc/recipes/prt.lua validate_state_transition_response and vg.lua
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'Off-chain verifiers (the C, Lua and JSON-RPC verify functions) | Support. A defect that the referee model in doc/recipes shows only through them is rated as theirs.')
candidates.location: src/replay-send-cmio-state-access.hpp check_read() lines 123-176 (checks type, address, log2_size, read data, read hash and proof, but never looks at access.get_written() / get_written_hash()); compare src/uarch-replay-state-access.hpp check_access_type() lines 150-165, which rejects 'unexpected written data' / 'unexpected written hash' on read accesses
candidates.description: For every read access of a send_cmio_response log (iflags.Y, htif.tohost, mcycle), the replay accepts arbitrary 'written' and 'written_hash' fields, even ones that disagree with the read data and with each other's role (a read cannot write). The uarch-step/reset replay rejects the same log defect. The extra fields do not change the after-hash, so the verifier turns a malformed log (R3 'inconsistent hashes', 'trailing data') into an acceptance instead of a rejection.
candidates.trigger: A dishonest player answering prove_state_transition at an input-boundary position in the recipe referee model (or anyone whose send_cmio log a node checks with the off-chain verifier) adds written/written_hash to a read access of send_cmio_log; the verifier still returns the honest after-hash.
candidates.reachability: Any honest delivery log can be decorated this way; no special machine state is needed. Reproduced on the baremetal-template configuration.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies (the trigger is a log from a dishonest claimant, which section 4 says is adversarial: 'A verifier must assume that every count, index, address, size, and hash it receives was chosen to fool it'). 2 Role: the defect is in the off-chain verify functions, role Support per AUDIT.md; the recipe referee model shows it only through them, so it is rated as theirs. 3 High/Medium cases: Medium lists 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3). A support verifier that does so is Low.' The data does not affect the result and the component is a support verifier, so this matches the Low clause; it is not 'accepting a wrong or second after-hash'. 4 Critical: no (no reachable-state rule broken on the honest operator's path; the on-chain SendCmioResponse.sol proof encoding has no written fields at all). 5 Low. Rule violated: R3 'Conditions on the log are validity conditions. A log that fails one must be rejected. Examples are ... trailing data, inconsistent hashes'.
candidates.threat_to_goal: No threat to the goal: the after-hash is unchanged and the deployed referee (Dave CartesiStateTransition with SendCmioResponse.sol) does not consume such fields. It is a validity-condition gap (R3) and an inconsistency between the two off-chain replay classes, which matters if the off-chain verifier is used as a reference (for example to reject malformed responses in the referee model).
candidates.evidence: Scratch script DFLOG/lowcase.lua: honest log_send_cmio_response on baremetal-template, set accesses[1].written = 32 x 0xff and written_hash = keccak256(written) on the read of iflags.Y; cartesi.machine:verify_send_cmio_response returns the honest after-hash (true, equal). The same mutation on a log_step_uarch log is rejected with 'unexpected written data in 1st access read access to uarch.cycle'. Also observed in the mutation fuzzer (DFLOG/fuzz.lua), op 6 on cmio read accesses was the only meaningful mutation class accepted.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: load baremetal-template, log_send_cmio_response with an ABI-encoded advance, add written/written_hash to a read access, call cartesi.machine:verify_send_cmio_response under pcall, and expect a rejection (exit 1 while it is accepted).

not_covered: Mutation fuzzing (about 12k mutated logs, plain and ASan+UBSan builds, logs with and without large data) covered verify_step_uarch, verify_reset_uarch (normal and rejection/revert path) and verify_send_cmio_response (accepting delivery and no-op delivery) through the Lua table -> JSON -> C++ path only; it found no crash, no sanitizer report and no accepted log with a different after-hash. Logs of uarch steps that execute the write-TLB ecall, misaligned or trap paths, and steps at uarch_cycle limits were not in the corpus (only the first ~60 uarch steps after a delivery).

The JSON-RPC server verify handlers were read but not fuzzed over the wire; the C API was probed only with deeply nested JSON (200k levels: no stack overflow, nlohmann 3.12 parser/destructor are iterative).

The on-chain proof encoding (prt-ethereum.lua append_log -> AccessLogs.sol/Buffer.sol) was checked by reading for field order and sibling counts against the C++ logs, not by an EVM differential fuzz; Buffer.peekBytes32 reads are unchecked but Dave's CartesiStateTransition requires exact consumption.
Proof (hash_tree_proof) JSON/Lua parsing paths and the Lua cartesi.hash-tree verify_slice used for computation-hash proofs (a neighbouring data flow, not logs).
Main-processor step logs (log_step/verify_step, binary format; ZK-only and out of scope).

Native write_unverified_tlb / mark_write_tlb_dirty_page behaviour on out-of-range TLB slot contents (a possible native-vs-replay trap divergence at another site than R1-R3-1) was noticed but not analysed.

Lua clua_get_array_table_len does not require dense arrays when a schema applies (a sparse Lua table with a huge integer key under AccessArray/Base64Array/NoteArray loops up to that key); not reachable from JSON-decoded player messages, so not reported, and not measured.
